=== HUNTRULE INTERFACE PUSHBACK ===

Your proposal:
```typescript
export interface HuntRule {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly cooldownMs: number;
  evaluate(curr: AttackerProfile, prev: AttackerProfile | null): { 
    match: boolean; 
    summary?: string; 
    severity?: 'info' | 'warn' | 'critical' 
  };
}
```

(I1) `{match: boolean, summary?, severity?}` splits 'did it fire' across two channels. When match=false, summary/severity are dead weight; when match=true, they're effectively required but the compiler can't enforce that. Counter-propose null-or-verdict — single channel, compiler enforces fields when verdict exists:
```typescript
import type { ThreatSeverity } from '../threat-monitor/signal-bus';

export interface RuleVerdict {
  severity: ThreatSeverity;
  summary: string;
  evidence: { ruleId: string; profileKey: string; counters: Record<string, number> };
}

export interface HuntRule {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly cooldownMs: number;
  readonly mode: 'on-mutation' | 'sweep' | 'both';
  evaluate(curr: AttackerProfile, prev: AttackerProfile | null): RuleVerdict | null;
}
```

(I2) Severity literal: use the `ThreatSeverity` import from signal-bus, not an inline literal. If we add a severity tier later (e.g. 'lethal' for Phase C bait-trigger), one source of truth.

(I3) No evidence field in your shape. The loop-protection convention is 'rule signals carry no identity-bearing evidence'. We need a field for evidence so the engine can populate it consistently — otherwise rules invent their own ad-hoc shapes and the source-prefix filter is the only thing standing between us and a feedback loop. Adding `evidence: { ruleId, profileKey, counters }` makes the contract explicit and lets the engine assert it before emitting.

(I4) The `mode` field — without it, persistence rule runs on every single mutation, wasting CPU on a check that only ever changes on the seconds-to-hours timescale. With mode, the engine can partition rules at construction time: mutation-hook runs on-mutation+both, sweep loop runs sweep+both.
